answer: Each identity runs one forge repair shop, locks 70 credits, and files one cipher-sealed repair record for a broken tool. A raven auditor load-tests the repaired tool against that record, burning the bond on a failed test. The k-th shop pays 35+3(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 3,032; 1,000 fakes pay 1,533,500 in fees plus 70,000 in bonds, with no sharing. A rented-repair ring fails: the same repaired tool carries the lender's cipher seal, so the raven key check burns both claims. An honest forge pays 70 once and 35 once, recovering the bond after a clean epoch.
